items.prompt:
Complete the statements.

Hoover Dam, completed in 1936, blocks the Colorado River to store water and produce electricity for cities and farms in the Southwest. Building the dam is an example of the geography theme {{0}}.

Geographers mapped every county in which more than half of the farmland is planted in corn. The area made up of those counties is an example of a {{1}}, because it is defined by a shared, measurable feature.

options: human-environment interaction
movement
relative location
place
why: Water and electricity do travel to cities, but the key action is changing the river itself. Movement is about how people, goods, and ideas travel.
Relative location describes where something is compared with other places. The statement is about changing a river, not describing where it is.
Place describes what an area is like. Building a dam is an action that changes the environment.

options: formal region
functional region
perceptual region
why: A functional region is organized around a central hub, such as a city's delivery area. These counties share a measured feature instead.
A perceptual region is based on people's feelings or opinions. The corn counties are defined by a measurement.

items.hint: For the first blank, ask whether people are changing nature. For the second, ask how the region's boundary was drawn.
items.explain:
Blank 1: human-environment interaction. Damming a river is people modifying the environment to meet their needs for water and power. "Movement" is tempting because water and electricity travel to cities, but the key action is changing the river itself.

Blank 2: formal region. A formal region is defined by a measurable feature shared across the area (more than half the farmland in corn). A functional region is organized around a hub, and a perceptual region is based on people's feelings about an area.

items.prompt: Based on the table, which country has a comparative advantage in producing cloth, and why?
options: Sudia, because it gives up 1 bushel of wheat for each bolt of cloth, while Norland gives up 2 bushels.
Norland, because one Norland worker can make more bolts of cloth per day than one Sudia worker can.
Norland, because it gives up only 1/2 bolt of cloth to grow each bushel of wheat that it produces.
Sudia, because one Sudia worker can produce exactly the same amount of wheat as of cloth each day.
why: Making more cloth (3 vs. 2) is absolute advantage. Comparative advantage depends on what is given up, and Norland gives up more wheat per bolt.
That is Norland's opportunity cost of wheat, not cloth. It shows Norland's comparative advantage is in wheat.
Sudia is the right country, but this is not a valid reason. Equal amounts of the two goods do not show which country gives up less.
items.hint: Find the opportunity cost of 1 bolt of cloth in each country: how much wheat is given up?
items.explain:
Norland: 6 wheat or 3 cloth, so 1 cloth costs 6 ÷ 3 = 2 bushels of wheat.
Sudia: 2 wheat or 2 cloth, so 1 cloth costs 2 ÷ 2 = 1 bushel of wheat.
Sudia gives up less wheat for each bolt of cloth, so Sudia has the comparative advantage in cloth.

Norland makes more cloth (3 vs. 2), but that is absolute advantage. The choice about Norland giving up 1/2 bolt describes the cost of wheat, which is why Norland's advantage is in wheat.

items.prompt: Which details from the passage support the claim that factory work in the late 1800s and early 1900s could be physically dangerous? Select two answers.
options: Machines had few safety guards, and workers lost fingers or hands in accidents.
Some exit doors had been locked, and 146 workers died in the Triangle fire.
The American Federation of Labor was founded in 1886.
Factories could make cloth, shoes, and steel more cheaply than skilled workers could.
The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 set a national minimum wage.
A typical factory employee worked six days a week.
why: The founding of the AFL is a fact about how workers organized. It says nothing about injuries or deaths.
This detail is about lower production costs, not about the safety of the workers.
The minimum wage is about pay, not physical danger, and it came decades later.
A six-day week shows the work was long and tiring, but it does not show that the work could injure or kill.
items.hint: Look for details about injuries or deaths, not about pay, hours, or laws.
items.explain:
The claim is about physical danger. Two details show it directly: machines without safety guards that cost workers fingers and hands (paragraph 2), and locked doors that contributed to 146 deaths in the Triangle fire (paragraph 4).

The six-day week is the most tempting wrong choice: it shows the work was exhausting, not that it caused injury or death.

items.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between people and the environment shown in the passage?
options: People removed the grass that held the soil, and when drought came, the damaged land drove many of them away.
The drought by itself caused the dust storms, and the way farmers had used the land played no part in them.
Farmers moved onto the Plains because earlier dust storms had made the topsoil of the region richer and deeper.
The government's soil programs caused the drought by changing the way that farmers plowed and planted their land.
why: The drought was natural, but the passage says "with the grass gone… nothing held the dry topsoil." Farming practices made the damage worse.
This reverses the order of events. Farmers plowed the Plains in the 1910s and 1920s; the dust storms came later, in the 1930s, and stripped the soil away.
The Soil Conservation Service was created in 1935, after the drought had begun, so it could not have caused it.
items.hint: Find two things in the passage: something people did to the land, and something the land then did to people.
items.explain:
The passage describes a two-way chain. First, people modified the environment: farmers plowed up the deep-rooted grasses that held the soil. Then the changed environment affected people: during the drought, nothing held the soil, dust storms followed, and many families lost their farms and migrated west.

The most tempting wrong answer says the drought alone caused the storms, but the passage clearly ties the storms to the missing grass.

items.skill: Direction and hemispheres on a map grid
items.prompt: A small plane flies in a straight line from Dunmore to Port Alder. Which statement accurately describes the flight?
options: The plane flies northwest and crosses both the equator and the prime meridian.
The plane flies northwest and crosses the equator but not the prime meridian.
The plane flies northeast and crosses both the equator and the prime meridian.
The plane flies southwest and crosses the prime meridian but not the equator.
why: Longitude changes from 4°E to 4°W, so the plane also crosses the prime meridian.
Port Alder is to the left of Dunmore on the grid, which is west, not east.
Dunmore is south of the equator and Port Alder is north of it, so the plane flies north and crosses the equator.
items.hint: Write the coordinates of both towns first. Did the latitude change from S to N? Did the longitude change from E to W?
items.explain:
Step 1: Dunmore is at 2°S, 4°E. Port Alder is at 2°N, 4°W.
Step 2: South to north is moving north; east to west is moving west. Together that is northwest.
Step 3: The latitude letter changes from S to N, so the plane crosses the equator. The longitude letter changes from E to W, so it also crosses the prime meridian.

"Northeast" comes from mixing up east and west.

items.prompt: Which conclusion about trade between Norland and Sudia is best supported by the table?
options: Both countries can gain if Norland specializes in wheat, Sudia specializes in cloth, and they trade.
Norland cannot gain from trade, because its workers produce more of both goods than Sudia's workers.
Sudia should specialize in wheat, because it gives up less cloth to grow wheat than Norland does.
Only Sudia can gain from trade with Norland, because Sudia is the less productive of the two countries.
why: This is the classic misconception that comparative advantage disproves. Producing more of both goods (absolute advantage) does not stop a country from gaining by trade.
Sudia gives up more cloth per bushel of wheat (1 bolt) than Norland (1/2 bolt), so Sudia should specialize in cloth, not wheat.
Trade based on comparative advantage benefits both sides, not only the less productive one.
items.hint: Find each country's opportunity cost for both goods. Each country should make the good it gives up the least to produce.
items.explain:
Opportunity cost of 1 bushel of wheat: Norland gives up 3 ÷ 6 = 1/2 bolt of cloth; Sudia gives up 2 ÷ 2 = 1 bolt. Norland has the comparative advantage in wheat.
Opportunity cost of 1 bolt of cloth: Norland gives up 2 bushels; Sudia gives up 1 bushel. Sudia has the comparative advantage in cloth.

When each country specializes in its comparative advantage and trades, both can end up with more than they could make alone. The idea that Norland cannot gain because it is better at both goods confuses absolute advantage with comparative advantage.

items.prompt: According to the excerpts, why did Congress decide to protect workers' right to organize and bargain collectively?
options: It found that unequal bargaining power hurt commerce and that protecting organizing would help restore balance.
It found that every employer should pay all of its workers the same wage, no matter what work they did.
It found that strikes burdened commerce, so it decided that workers should no longer be allowed to strike.
It found that businesses organized as corporations were illegal and should be broken into smaller firms.
why: The excerpts never mention equal wages for all jobs. They say unequal bargaining power depresses wage rates, which is a different idea.
The excerpts say strikes come from employers denying the right to organize. Congress's answer was to protect organizing, not to ban strikes.

The phrase "organized in the corporate… forms" describes how employers are organized; it does not call corporations illegal. Breaking up business combinations is the idea behind the Sherman Antitrust Act.
items.hint: Find the phrase "restoring equality" in the last excerpt. What problem does it solve?
items.explain:
The second excerpt says the "inequality of bargaining power" between workers and corporate employers "burdens… the flow of commerce" and depresses wages. The third says protecting the right to organize "promotes the flow of commerce" by "restoring equality of bargaining power." So Congress protected organizing to restore balance and help commerce.

The strike choice is tempting because the first excerpt mentions strikes, but it blames strikes on employers who refuse to bargain; the law's solution is to protect bargaining, not to outlaw strikes.

items.prompt: Corvalia had a trade deficit in every year shown. By how many billion dollars did Corvalia's trade deficit shrink from 2022 to 2024?

mistakes.why: You found the change in exports (66 − 55). First find each year's deficit (imports − exports), then compare the two deficits.
You found the change in imports (71 − 68). First find each year's deficit: 2022 is 71 − 55 = 16 and 2024 is 68 − 66 = 2.
You added the two deficits (16 + 2). To find how much the deficit shrank, subtract: 16 − 2.

items.hint: Find the deficit for 2022 and for 2024 first (imports minus exports), then compare them.
items.explain:
2022 deficit: imports − exports = 71 − 55 = $16 billion.
2024 deficit: 68 − 66 = $2 billion.
Change: 16 − 2 = $14 billion smaller.

Subtracting only exports (66 − 55 = 11) or only imports (71 − 68 = 3) skips the step of finding each year's deficit.

items.skill: Cause and effect in economic history
items.prompt: According to the passage, why did members of the American Railway Union refuse to work on trains that included Pullman cars?
options: To support Pullman workers whose wages had been cut while their rents stayed the same.
Because a federal court had ordered them to stop working on trains that carried those cars.
To pressure Congress into making Labor Day a national holiday for all American workers.
Because Pullman cars had been banned from trains that carried the United States mail.
why: This reverses the order of events. The court order came after the boycott began, and it ordered union leaders to stop interfering with trains, not to stop working.
The passage says Congress created Labor Day while the boycott was under way, but it never says the holiday was the boycott's goal.
The passage never says Pullman cars were banned. The injunction was about union leaders interfering with mail trains.
items.hint: Paragraph 3 says the boycott was "in support of" someone. Who, and what had happened to them in paragraph 2?
items.explain:
Paragraph 2 says the company cut wages by 20 to 30 percent but "did not lower the rents." Paragraph 3 says the ARU began its boycott "in support of the Pullman workers." So the boycott supported workers whose pay was cut while their rents stayed the same.

The court-order choice reverses cause and effect: the injunction was the government's response to the boycott.

options: Ridgeway
Hollis

Easton
why: Hollis is at 3°N, 2°E. Choosing it means the numbers were reversed by reading across first, as in (x, y). Latitude, the N number, comes first.
Marston is at 2°S, 3°E. The longitude is right, but Marston is below the equator, which is south, not north.
Easton is at 2°N, 3°W. The latitude is right, but Easton is to the left of the prime meridian, which is west, not east.
items.hint: Latitude comes first. Go 2 lines up from the equator, then 3 lines right of the prime meridian.
items.explain:
Step 1: 2°N means 2 lines above the equator.
Step 2: 3°E means 3 lines right of the prime meridian.
Step 3: The town at that point is Ridgeway.

Hollis (3°N, 2°E) is the most common wrong answer: it comes from reversing the numbers.

items.prompt: Drag each reason for migrating into the correct category.
choices: A long drought turns a family's fields to dust.
A shipyard in a coastal city is hiring welders.
Soldiers burn villages during a civil war.
A new country offers citizenship to trained nurses.
Government officials arrest reporters who criticize them.
Cousins abroad send letters praising the schools in their town.
items.why: The most common mistake is calling the cousins' letters a push factor because the letters encouraged the move. The letters praise the new place, so they describe a pull factor.
items.hint: Ask: Is this a problem with the place people are leaving, or an attraction of the place they are going?
items.explain:
Push factors (problems in the old place): the drought, the burning of villages in the civil war, and the arrests of reporters.

Pull factors (attractions of the new place): shipyard jobs, citizenship for nurses, and the good schools the cousins describe.

items.prompt: A new law says that no more than 40,000 tons of foreign beef may be imported into the country each year. What kind of trade policy is this?
options: A quota
A tariff
An embargo
A free-trade agreement
why: A tariff is a tax on imports. This law does not tax the beef; it limits how much may enter.
An embargo bans trade completely. Here up to 40,000 tons may still be imported.
A free-trade agreement lowers barriers. A cap on imports is a barrier, not the removal of one.
items.hint: Is the policy a tax, a limit on the amount, or a complete ban?
items.explain: A limit on the amount of a good that may be imported is a quota. A tariff would tax the beef, an embargo would ban it, and a free-trade agreement would remove barriers instead of adding one.

items.prompt: Which statement is supported by the graph?
options: The factory share of workers fell between 1920 and 1930 and then rose again by 1940.
The factory share of workers rose in every one of the ten-year periods shown on the graph.
By the 1900 census, most workers in Ashford County were already employed in factories.
The largest ten-year increase in the factory share came between the 1930 and 1940 censuses.
why: Check every decade: the share dropped from 38% in 1920 to 34% in 1930, so it did not rise in every period.
In 1900 the factory share was 24%, less than half. "Most" would require more than 50%.
The 1930–1940 increase was 40 − 34 = 6 points. Three earlier decades rose by 7 points each (1890–1900, 1900–1910, 1910–1920).
items.hint: Write down all seven values, then check each ten-year change.
items.explain:
The values are 12, 17, 24, 31, 38, 34, and 40. The share fell from 38% (1920) to 34% (1930), then rose to 40% (1940). That matches the correct statement.

Because of the 1920–1930 drop, the share did not rise every decade. In 1900 only 24% worked in factories. The 1930–1940 increase (6 points) was smaller than the 7-point increases in 1890–1900, 1900–1910, and 1910–1920.

items.explain:
1920 value: 38%
1880 value: 12%
Change: 38 − 12 = 26 percentage points.

items.prompt:
Complete the statements.

Farmers in a dry desert valley dig canals to carry water from a river to their fields. Digging the canals is an example of the geography theme {{0}}.

The area that receives the broadcast signal of one city's television station is an example of a {{1}}, because it is organized around a central hub.

options: human-environment interaction
movement
relative location
place
why: Water does move through the canals, but the key action is people changing the land and river to meet their needs. Movement is about how people, goods, and ideas travel.
Relative location describes where something is compared with other places. The statement is about changing the land, not describing where it is.
Place describes what an area is like. Digging canals is an action that changes the environment.

options: functional region
formal region
perceptual region
why: A formal region shares a measurable feature, such as a climate. The station's area is defined by a hub, the station.
A perceptual region is based on people's feelings or opinions. The broadcast area is defined by the reach of the station.

items.hint: For the first blank, ask whether people are changing nature. For the second, ask what defines the region's edge.
items.explain:
Blank 1: human-environment interaction. Digging irrigation canals is people modifying the environment. "Movement" is tempting because water flows through the canals, but the key action is changing the land and river.

Blank 2: functional region. The broadcast area is organized around a hub (the station). A formal region shares a measurable feature, and a perceptual region is based on people's feelings about an area.

items.prompt: Based on the table, which country has a comparative advantage in producing coffee, and why?
options: Marisol, because each sack of coffee costs it 1/4 of a bicycle, while each sack costs Tavia 1/2 of a bicycle.
Tavia, because one Tavia worker can grow more sacks of coffee each day than one Marisol worker can grow.
Tavia, because it gives up only 2 sacks of coffee to build each bicycle, while Marisol gives up 4 sacks.
Marisol, because one Marisol worker can produce more sacks of coffee each day than bicycles each day.
why: Growing more coffee (12 vs. 8) is absolute advantage. Comparative advantage depends on what is given up for each sack.
That is the opportunity cost of a bicycle, not of coffee. It shows Tavia's comparative advantage is in bicycles.
Marisol is the right country, but this is not a valid reason. Comparing a country's own two outputs does not show what it gives up compared with Tavia.
items.hint: Find the opportunity cost of 1 sack of coffee in each country: how many bicycles are given up?
items.explain:
Tavia: 12 coffee or 6 bicycles, so 1 sack of coffee costs 6 ÷ 12 = 1/2 bicycle.
Marisol: 8 coffee or 2 bicycles, so 1 sack costs 2 ÷ 8 = 1/4 bicycle.
Marisol gives up less for each sack, so Marisol has the comparative advantage in coffee.

Tavia grows more coffee per worker, but that is absolute advantage. The "2 sacks per bicycle" figure is the cost of a bicycle, which is why Tavia's advantage is in bicycles.

items.prompt: Which details from the passage support the claim that the federal government sided with the railroads during the Pullman Strike? Select two answers.
options: A federal court forbade the union's leaders from interfering with trains that carried the mail.
President Cleveland sent federal troops to Chicago even though the governor of Illinois objected.
The Pullman company cut wages by 20 to 30 percent but did not lower the rents in its town.
About 250,000 workers in 27 states took part in the boycott at its peak.
Congress voted to make Labor Day a national holiday while the boycott was under way.
Many of the strikers belonged to the American Railway Union, led by Eugene V. Debs.
why: This is an action by the Pullman company, not by the federal government.
This detail shows the size of the boycott. It says nothing about the government taking a side.
Creating a holiday honoring workers is a step toward workers, not a sign of siding with the railroads.
This identifies the union and its leader. It does not describe any government action.
items.hint: Look only for actions taken by a federal court, the President, or Congress. Then ask which ones helped the railroads.
items.explain:
The claim is about the federal government taking the railroads' side. Two details show it: a federal court's injunction against the union's leaders (paragraph 4), and President Cleveland's decision to send federal troops over the governor's objection (paragraph 4).

The wage cut is tempting because it is unfair to workers, but it was the company's action, not the government's. The Labor Day law points the other way.

items.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between people and the environment shown in the passage?
options: People reshaped the river with dams to control floods and make power, which helped many residents but displaced others.
Floods forced people to abandon the valley for good, so the government chose to leave the river in its natural condition.
People adapted to the floods only by moving their homes to higher ground, without making any changes to the river itself.
The dams changed the river's flow, but they had no effect on where people in the valley lived or how they earned a living.
why: The passage says the TVA built dams on the river; the government changed the river rather than leaving it alone.
The passage describes dams that changed the river. That is modifying the environment, not only adapting to it.
Paragraphs 3 and 4 say the dams brought electricity and factories and forced thousands of families to move.
items.hint: Find something people did to the river, then find two effects that change had on people.
items.explain:
The TVA modified the environment: it built dams that "held back floodwaters, deepened the river for barges, and used falling water to generate electricity" (paragraph 2). The changed river then affected people in two ways: electricity and factories helped many residents (paragraph 3), while the lakes behind the dams forced thousands of families to move (paragraph 4).

The choice saying the dams had no effect on where people lived ignores paragraph 4.

items.prompt: A supply truck drives in a straight line from Pine Bluff to Tolland. Which statement accurately describes the trip?
options: The truck travels southeast and crosses both the equator and the prime meridian.
The truck travels northeast and crosses both the equator and the prime meridian.
The truck travels southeast and crosses the prime meridian but not the equator.
The truck travels southwest and crosses the equator but not the prime meridian.
why: Tolland is below the equator and Pine Bluff is above it, so the truck travels south, not north.
Latitude changes from 4°N to 3°S, so the truck also crosses the equator.
Tolland is to the right of Pine Bluff on the grid, which is east, and longitude changes from W to E, so the prime meridian is crossed too.
items.hint: Write the coordinates of both towns first. Did the latitude letter change? Did the longitude letter change?
items.explain:
Step 1: Pine Bluff is at 4°N, 5°W. Tolland is at 3°S, 5°E.
Step 2: North to south is moving south; west to east is moving east. Together that is southeast.
Step 3: The latitude letter changes from N to S, so the truck crosses the equator. The longitude letter changes from W to E, so it also crosses the prime meridian.

"Northeast" comes from mixing up north and south.

items.prompt: Which conclusion about trade between Tavia and Marisol is best supported by the table?
options: Both countries can gain if Tavia specializes in bicycles, Marisol specializes in coffee, and they trade.
Tavia cannot gain from trade, because its workers produce more of both goods than Marisol's workers.
Marisol should specialize in bicycles, because it gives up less coffee to build a bicycle than Tavia does.
Only Marisol can gain from trade with Tavia, because Marisol is the less productive of the two countries.
why: This is the classic misconception. Producing more of both goods (absolute advantage) does not stop a country from gaining by trade.
Marisol gives up more coffee per bicycle (4 sacks) than Tavia (2 sacks), so Marisol should specialize in coffee.
Trade based on comparative advantage benefits both sides, not only the less productive one.
items.hint: Find each country's opportunity cost for both goods. Each country should make the good it gives up the least to produce.
items.explain:
Opportunity cost of 1 bicycle: Tavia gives up 12 ÷ 6 = 2 sacks of coffee; Marisol gives up 8 ÷ 2 = 4 sacks. Tavia has the comparative advantage in bicycles.
Opportunity cost of 1 sack of coffee: Tavia gives up 1/2 bicycle; Marisol gives up 1/4 bicycle. Marisol has the comparative advantage in coffee.

When each country specializes in its comparative advantage and trades, both can gain. Saying Tavia cannot gain because it is better at both goods confuses absolute advantage with comparative advantage.

items.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the main argument of the excerpt?
options: Government should set limits on working hours and child labor and guarantee a minimum wage.
Private businesses can end low wages and long hours on their own, without any new laws.
The nation lacks the natural resources it would need to pay all of its workers a fair wage.
Labor unions, rather than the government, should decide the hours and wages of all workers.
why: This reverses the excerpt. Roosevelt says "government must have some control" over hours, wages, and child labor.
This reverses the excerpt. Roosevelt calls the nation "so richly endowed with natural resources" that it should be able to pay fair wages.
The excerpt mentions "unorganized labor" only as workers who are exploited. Its solution is government control, not unions in place of government.
items.hint: Find the sentence that says what "government must" do.
items.explain:
Roosevelt argues that the nation can afford "a fair day's pay for a fair day's work," that there is "no justification" for child labor, low wages, or long hours, and that "government must have some control over maximum hours, minimum wages, the evil of child labor." That is a call for laws like the Fair Labor Standards Act, which Congress passed in 1938.

The choices about private businesses and natural resources both reverse what the excerpt says.

items.prompt: Pradera had a trade surplus in 2021 and a trade deficit in 2024. By how many billion dollars did Pradera's trade balance (exports − imports) fall from 2021 to 2024?

mistakes.why: You found 13 − 7. A move from a $7 billion surplus to a $13 billion deficit crosses zero, so the two amounts add: 7 + 13.
You found the change in exports only (80 − 79). First find each year's balance, exports minus imports.
You found the change in imports only (93 − 72). First find each year's balance, exports minus imports.

items.hint: Find the balance (exports minus imports) for each year. One is positive and one is negative.
items.explain:
2021 balance: 79 − 72 = +$7 billion (a surplus).
2024 balance: 80 − 93 = −$13 billion (a deficit).
Change: 7 − (−13) = 7 + 13 = $20 billion. The balance fell by $20 billion.

stimuli.title: Reading: Tomas Novak Leaves Home
stimuli.html:
The Novak family is fictional, but their story is typical of millions of immigrants from eastern and southern Europe around 1900.

(1) In 1907, Tomas Novak, age 22, left his village in the hills of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. His father's small farm had been divided among the sons so many times that Tomas's share could not feed a family. Two poor harvests in a row had left the family in debt, and Tomas also faced years of required service in the army.

(2) That spring, a letter arrived from his cousin Pavel in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The steel mills there were hiring, Pavel wrote, and a laborer could earn more in a day than a farmhand at home earned in a week. A neighbor who had come back from America described a boardinghouse near the mills where newcomers from their region lived together and spoke their own language.

(3) Tomas found work in a Pittsburgh mill within a week. The shifts were twelve hours long, the furnaces were dangerous, and he missed his family. Still, by 1910 he had saved enough to send for his younger brother.

stimuli.title: Reading: The Harlan Family Heads West
stimuli.html:
The Harlan family is fictional, but their story is typical of the families who left the southern Great Plains during the Dust Bowl.

(1) By 1936, the Harlans had farmed wheat in Cimarron County, Oklahoma, for twenty years. For three straight years, dust storms had buried their fences and killed their wheat before it could ripen. Without a crop to sell, they could not make the payments on their farm loan, and that spring the bank took the farm.

(2) At the general store, Ruth Harlan picked up a printed handbill announcing that growers in California needed thousands of workers to pick peas and cotton. A week later, a letter came from her brother in Bakersfield, California, saying the family could stay in his spare room until they found work.

(3) The Harlans packed their truck and drove west on Route 66. The truck broke down twice in the desert, and the trip took eleven days. In California they found work in the fields, though the pay was low and the jobs lasted only as long as each harvest.

items.prompt: The first transcontinental railroad was completed in 1869. Which effect would this event most likely have had?
options: Farms and factories in the West could ship goods to Eastern cities faster and more cheaply.
Fewer people moved west, because crossing the country now took longer than it had before.
Eastern factories lost customers, because their goods could no longer reach Western towns.
Barges began carrying goods on the Erie Canal between the Great Lakes and New York City.
why: This reverses the effect. A railroad made crossing the country much faster, which encouraged people to move west.
This reverses the effect. The railroad connected the East and West, so Eastern goods could reach Western towns more easily.
This mixes up the timeline. The Erie Canal opened in 1825, more than forty years before the railroad, and it was not caused by it.
items.explain:
A railroad linking East and West cut travel time and shipping costs, so goods could move between the regions faster and more cheaply. That widened markets for both Western farms and Eastern factories.

The Erie Canal choice is a true event but the wrong cause and time: the canal opened in 1825.

items.prompt: In 1937, a textile mill paid workers 15 cents an hour and employed 13-year-olds for 60-hour weeks. Which law passed in 1938 was designed to address these conditions?
options: The Fair Labor Standards Act
The National Labor Relations Act
The Sherman Antitrust Act
The Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act
why: The National Labor Relations Act (Wagner Act, 1935) protected the right to form unions. It did not set a minimum wage or limit child labor, and it came before 1938.
The Sherman Antitrust Act (1890) outlawed business combinations that limited competition. It did not deal with wages or child labor.
The Smoot-Hawley Tariff (1930) raised taxes on imports. It had nothing to do with wages, hours, or child labor.
items.explain: The Fair Labor Standards Act (1938) set a federal minimum wage of 25 cents an hour, required overtime pay for long workweeks, and restricted child labor, which matches all three problems in the mill. The Wagner Act (1935) is the most tempting wrong answer, but it protected the right to organize, not wages and hours.

items.prompt: Based on the table, which country has the comparative advantage in producing fish? Type the country's name.

mistakes.why: Galen catches more fish (5 vs. 4), but that is absolute advantage. A crate of fish costs Galen 15 ÷ 5 = 3 tons of lumber and costs Moravia only 8 ÷ 4 = 2 tons.

items.explain:
Cost of 1 crate of fish: Galen gives up 15 ÷ 5 = 3 tons of lumber. Moravia gives up 8 ÷ 4 = 2 tons of lumber.
Moravia gives up less, so Moravia has the comparative advantage in fish. (Galen has it in lumber: a ton costs Galen 1/3 crate but costs Moravia 1/2 crate.)

Galen produces more of both goods, but producing more is absolute advantage, not comparative advantage.

items.prompt: Over several centuries, people in the Netherlands built long walls of earth called dikes and pumped seawater off low-lying land to create new farmland. Which kind of human-environment interaction does this show?
options: Modifying the environment
Adapting to the environment
Depending on the environment
Movement of people and goods
why: Adapting means changing how people live or build to fit the land, as with houses on stilts. Building dikes and draining the sea changes the land itself.
Depending means using what nature already provides, such as fishing. Here people are creating new land.
Movement is a separate theme about how people, goods, and ideas travel. Nothing in the description is about travel.
items.explain: Building dikes and pumping out seawater physically changes the environment to create new land. That is modifying the environment. Adapting would mean changing how people live to fit the land without changing the land itself.

items.prompt:
Complete the statement.

Country Z places a new tariff on imported shoes. As a result, the price of imported shoes in Country Z will most likely {{0}}, and shoe manufacturers based in Country Z will most likely {{1}}.

options: rise
fall
stay the same
why: A tariff is a tax on imports. Taxes add to the importer's cost, which is usually passed on to buyers, so prices go up, not down.
The tariff adds a tax to every imported pair, so the cost of bringing shoes into the country increases, and the price usually rises with it.

options: sell more shoes
sell fewer shoes
stop making shoes
why: When imported shoes cost more, some buyers switch to shoes made at home, so domestic makers usually sell more, not fewer.
The tariff makes domestic shoes more competitive, not less. It protects home producers rather than driving them out.

items.explain:
Blank 1: rise. The tariff is a tax on imported shoes, which raises their cost, and sellers usually pass that on to buyers.

Blank 2: sell more shoes. With imports more expensive, some buyers switch to shoes made in Country Z, so domestic manufacturers gain. That is why tariffs are often described as protecting domestic producers.

items.prompt: Which details from the passage describe pull factors in Tomas Novak's decision to migrate? Select two answers.
options: Steel mills in Pittsburgh were hiring, and a laborer could earn more in a day than a farmhand at home earned in a week.
A boardinghouse near the mills housed newcomers from his region who spoke their own language.
His share of the family farm was too small to feed a family.
Two poor harvests in a row had left his family in debt.
He faced years of required service in the army.
The mill shifts were twelve hours long, and the furnaces were dangerous.
why: A farm too small to support a family is a problem in the old place, so it is a push factor.
Poor harvests and debt are problems at home, so they are push factors.
Required army service in his home country is a reason to leave, so it is a push factor.
Long, dangerous shifts are hardships of the new place. They did not attract Tomas; he learned about them after he arrived.
items.explain:
Pull factors are attractions of the new place. Two details describe Pittsburgh in a way that drew Tomas there: mills hiring at much higher pay and a boardinghouse where newcomers from his region lived together (paragraph 2).

The small farm, the poor harvests, and the army service are push factors (problems at home). The long, dangerous shifts are a hardship he found after arriving, not a reason he chose Pittsburgh.

items.prompt: Which statement is supported by the graph?
options: Varena had a trade surplus in 2019 and 2023 and a trade deficit in each of the years between.
Varena's exports fell in at least one of the years shown, even though its imports kept rising.
Varena's largest trade deficit shown, $4 billion, came in 2022, the year its imports peaked.
Varena's trade deficits were caused by other countries placing tariffs on Varena's exports.
why: Check the export bars: 42, 45, 47, 51, 54. Exports rose every year. (Imports were the series that fell once, from 55 to 53.)
In 2022 the deficit was 55 − 51 = $4 billion, but in 2021 it was 52 − 47 = $5 billion. The year with the highest imports did not have the largest deficit.
The graph shows the amounts of trade, not the reasons for them. Nothing on it is about tariffs.
items.explain:
Balance each year (exports − imports): 2019: 42 − 40 = +2 (surplus); 2020: 45 − 46 = −1; 2021: 47 − 52 = −5; 2022: 51 − 55 = −4; 2023: 54 − 53 = +1 (surplus). So Varena had surpluses in 2019 and 2023 and deficits from 2020 through 2022.

The tempting wrong answer picks 2022 because imports were highest that year, but the deficit depends on the gap between the bars, which was largest in 2021.

items.prompt: The Erie Canal opened in 1825, linking the Great Lakes to the Hudson River and New York City by water. Which effect would this event most likely have had?
options: More goods from the Great Lakes region passed through New York City's port, and the city's trade grew.
Shipping goods between the Great Lakes and the Atlantic coast became slower and more costly than before.
Farmers near the Great Lakes lost their access to buyers in Eastern cities such as New York City.
The first railroad across the continent was completed and joined the Atlantic and Pacific coasts.
why: This reverses the effect. A water route was cheaper than hauling goods overland by wagon, so shipping became faster and less costly.
This reverses the effect. The canal gave Great Lakes farmers a cheap route to Eastern buyers.
This mixes up the timeline. The transcontinental railroad was completed in 1869, more than forty years later.
items.explain: The canal created a cheap water route between the Great Lakes and New York City, so more goods flowed through New York's port and the city's trade grew. The railroad choice is a true event but the wrong time: it was completed in 1869.

items.prompt: In 1934, a factory fired every worker who joined a union and refused to meet with union leaders. Which law passed in 1935 was designed to stop practices like these?

The Fair Labor Standards Act
The Sherman Antitrust Act
The Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act
why: The Fair Labor Standards Act (1938) set a minimum wage, overtime, and child labor limits. It did not deal with the right to join a union, and it came after 1935.
The Sherman Antitrust Act (1890) outlawed business combinations that limited competition, not the firing of union members.
The Smoot-Hawley Tariff (1930) raised taxes on imports. It had nothing to do with unions.
items.explain: The National Labor Relations Act (Wagner Act, 1935) protected workers' right to form unions and required employers to bargain with them, which addresses both firing union members and refusing to meet. The Fair Labor Standards Act is the most tempting wrong answer, but it dealt with wages, hours, and child labor.

Cost of 1 lamp: Ferro gives up 24 ÷ 6 = 4 rugs. Lusan gives up 10 ÷ 5 = 2 rugs.
Lusan gives up less, so Lusan has the comparative advantage in lamps. (Ferro has it in rugs: a rug costs Ferro 1/4 lamp but costs Lusan 1/2 lamp.)

Ferro produces more of both goods, but that is absolute advantage, not comparative advantage.

items.prompt: In a hot desert city, families build homes with thick walls and small windows, and many people do outdoor work in the early morning before the heat peaks. Which kind of human-environment interaction does this show?
options: Adapting to the environment
Modifying the environment
Depending on the environment
Movement of people and goods
why: Modifying means changing the land or water itself, as with a dam. Thick walls and early work hours change how people live, not the desert.
Depending means using what nature provides, such as farming fertile soil. These people are protecting themselves from the heat.
Movement is a separate theme about how people, goods, and ideas travel. Nothing in the description is about travel.
items.explain: Thick walls, small windows, and early work hours change how people build and live so they fit the hot climate, without changing the desert itself. That is adapting to the environment.

Complete the statement.

Country W sets a quota that cuts the amount of sugar that may be imported each year in half. With less foreign sugar for sale, the price of sugar in Country W will most likely {{0}}, and sugar growers in Country W will most likely {{1}}.

options: rise
fall
stay the same
why: A quota reduces the supply of sugar. When supply falls and demand does not, the price goes up, not down.
Cutting imports in half reduces the supply of sugar for sale. Less supply with the same demand pushes the price up.

options: benefit
be harmed
stop growing sugar
why: With less foreign competition and higher prices, domestic growers can sell more sugar at a better price, so they gain.
The quota protects domestic growers from foreign competition. It gives them more reason to grow sugar, not less.

items.prompt: On the grid, the horizontal axis is the equator and the vertical axis is the prime meridian. Each line is 1 degree. Click the point at 4°S, 3°E.
items.why: The most common wrong click is 4 lines right and 3 lines down, which reverses latitude and longitude (that point is 3°S, 4°E). The S number, 4, moves you down.
items.explain:
4°S is latitude: move 4 lines down from the equator. 3°E is longitude: move 3 lines right of the prime meridian. The point is 3 right and 4 down.

Clicking 4 right and 3 down reverses the coordinates. Clicking 3 left and 4 down uses west instead of east.

items.prompt: Which details from the passage describe push factors in the Harlan family's decision to migrate? Select two answers.
options: For three straight years, dust storms had buried their fences and killed their wheat.
The bank took the farm after the family could not make its loan payments.
A handbill announced that California growers needed thousands of pickers.
Ruth's brother in Bakersfield offered the family his spare room.
The truck broke down twice in the desert during the eleven-day trip.
In California, the field jobs lasted only as long as each harvest.
why: Jobs in California are an attraction of the new place, so this is a pull factor.
A relative offering a place to stay makes California more attractive. That is a pull factor.
A breakdown on the road is a hardship of the journey. It is not a reason the family left Oklahoma.
Short-lived jobs are a hardship the family found after arriving. They are not a reason for leaving Oklahoma.
items.explain:
Push factors are problems in the place people leave. Two details describe Oklahoma: dust storms that killed the wheat and the bank taking the farm (paragraph 1).

The handbill and the brother's offer are pull factors. The truck breakdowns and short-lived jobs are hardships of the trip and the new place, not reasons for leaving.

items.prompt: Which statement is supported by the graph?
options: Kerrow had a trade deficit in 2019, 2020, and 2021 and a trade surplus in 2022 and 2023.
Kerrow's imports rose in every year shown, while its exports rose in only some of the years.
Kerrow's largest trade surplus shown, $6 billion, came in 2021, the year with the widest gap.
Kerrow's trade surpluses in 2022 and 2023 were caused by a new free-trade agreement.
why: Check the import bars: 35, 34, 37, 35, 38. Imports fell in 2020 and in 2022, so they did not rise every year.
2021 did have the widest gap, but Kerrow imported more than it exported (37 vs. 31), so the $6 billion gap was a deficit, not a surplus.
The graph shows the amounts of trade, not the reasons for them. Nothing on it is about trade agreements.
items.explain:
Balance each year (exports − imports): 2019: 30 − 35 = −5; 2020: 33 − 34 = −1; 2021: 31 − 37 = −6; 2022: 36 − 35 = +1; 2023: 40 − 38 = +2. So Kerrow had deficits from 2019 through 2021 and surpluses in 2022 and 2023.

The tempting wrong answer calls 2021's $6 billion gap a surplus; because imports were larger, it was a deficit.

vocab.def: The shift from making goods by hand to making them with machines in factories.
vocab.example: Industrialization drew thousands of farm workers to mill towns such as Lowell, Massachusetts.

vocab.def: An organization of workers that bargains with employers as a group.
vocab.example: The union asked the factory owner for safer machines and a shorter workday.

vocab.def: Talks between a union and an employer about wages, hours, and working conditions.
vocab.example: After weeks of collective bargaining, the workers won a 5% raise.

vocab.def: A refusal by workers to work until their demands are met.
vocab.example: The railroad workers went on strike when their wages were cut.

vocab.def: What you give up when you choose to use resources for one thing instead of another.
vocab.example: If a worker makes 1 pie instead of 2 loaves of bread, the opportunity cost of the pie is 2 loaves.

vocab.def: The ability to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than someone else.
vocab.example: Bora has a comparative advantage in shirts because it gives up fewer radios to make each shirt.

vocab.def: A tariff is a tax on imported goods; a quota is a limit on how much of a good can be imported; an embargo is a ban on trade with a country.
vocab.example: A tariff on imported steel raised the price of steel for car makers.

vocab.def: An export is a good sold to another country; an import is a good bought from another country.
vocab.example: The United States exports soybeans and imports coffee.

vocab.def: A trade deficit means a country imports more than it exports; a trade surplus means it exports more than it imports.
vocab.example: A country that exports $80 billion and imports $95 billion has a trade deficit of $15 billion.

vocab.def: Distance north or south of the equator, measured in degrees from 0° to 90°.
vocab.example: A city at 30°N is 30 degrees north of the equator.

vocab.def: Distance east or west of the prime meridian, measured in degrees from 0° to 180°.
vocab.example: A city at 90°W is 90 degrees west of the prime meridian.

vocab.def: An area that shares one or more features, such as climate, language, landforms, or economic activity.
vocab.example: The Great Plains is a region of flat grassland used for farming and ranching.

vocab.def: The ways people depend on, adapt to, and change their natural surroundings.
vocab.example: Building a dam to store water for a desert city is human-environment interaction.

vocab.def: The movement of people from one place to another to live.
vocab.example: During the Great Migration, millions of African Americans moved from the rural South to Northern cities.

vocab.def: Push factors are reasons people leave a place; pull factors are reasons they move to a new place.
vocab.example: A drought (push) and factory jobs in a city (pull) can both lead a farm family to move.

notes:
Week 8 Study Sheet: Economics in History and Geography

Industrialization and Labor

  • Industrial Revolution: began in Great Britain, late 1700s; reached U.S. about 1790
  • 1825 Erie Canal; 1869 transcontinental railroad
  • 1886 American Federation of Labor; 1890 Sherman Antitrust Act
  • 1894 Pullman Strike: court injunction and federal troops break the strike
  • 1911 Triangle fire (146 killed) → safety laws
  • 1935 Wagner Act: right to unionize; 1938 Fair Labor Standards Act: minimum wage, overtime, child labor limits
  • 1920: first census with more than half of Americans urban

Trade

  • Export = sell abroad; import = buy from abroad
  • Opportunity cost = what you give up
  • Comparative advantage = lower opportunity cost → specialize in it
  • Tariff = tax on imports (raises prices); quota = limit; embargo = ban
  • Trade deficit: imports > exports; surplus: exports > imports
  • Opportunity cost of 1 X = Y made ÷ X made
  • Tariff effects: domestic producers gain; buyers pay more; other countries may retaliate

Five Themes of Geography

  • Location (absolute / relative)
  • Place
  • Human-environment interaction: depend, adapt, modify
  • Movement
  • Region: formal (measurable feature), functional (hub), perceptual (feelings)

Migration

  • Push = reason to leave (war, drought, persecution)
  • Pull = reason to go (jobs, family, freedom)
  • Great Migration: about 6 million African Americans, South → North, Midwest, West (about 1910–1970)
  • Dust Bowl (1930s): plowed grasslands + drought → dust storms → migration west

Reading data: subtract two percents to get percentage points; percent change = change ÷ starting value × 100. A graph shows what changed, not why.

GED tip: On map questions, check both the numbers and the direction letters. On trade questions, compare what is given up, not just what is made.
